newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-ARROWS PAIR PUNISHED FOR DANGEROUS DRIVING.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ARROWS PAIR PUNISHED FOR DANGEROUS DRIVING.

text.p: World champion Damon Hill of Britain and Arrows team mate Pedro Diniz of Brazil were given one-race bans, suspended for one race, for dangerous driving during Sunday's San Marino Grand Prix.
Hill, who crashed out of the race in a collision with Japan's Shinji Nakano, was found guilty by the race stewards of causing an avoidable collision after an investigation into the incident.
Nakano, driving a Prost, was speared off the track by Hill's Arrows car and said later that he found the entire incident incredible.
He said: "Mr World Champion hit me, pushed me off and that finished my race. I dont want to say anything. It was just incredible."
Hill admitted he had "T-boned him" in the accident and took the blame for his own impetuous driving, in trying to make up ground from the back of the field.
He had been forced to start the race from the pit lane because of an oil leak the Arrows team discovered on his car on the grid.

Before he left the circuit, Hill said: "I tried to pass him, but he just turned in on me. I had too much to make up as I had started from the pit lane and I was held up badly by the guys in front of me."
Diniz was given a similar ban for not observing blue flags when a near-collision with Canadian Jacques Villeneuve's Williams took place early in the race.
